summary: For a West Kelowna business, compare Michael McKerracher for hands-on websites, content and marketing; Twin Creek Media for an ongoing marketing partnership; TheBomb for custom websites with hosting and support; and Twirling Umbrellas for more involved WordPress projects. Match the provider to the customer journey and the support you will need after launch.
takeaways: Describe the exact customer journey: service enquiry, visitor booking or organisational resource.
Ask each provider to walk through the complete booking or enquiry handoff on mobile.
Use local project relevance, content ownership and after-launch support to narrow the shortlist.

sections.body:
I work with West Kelowna business owners who want one person to connect the design, words and practical setup of their website. I’m based in Coldstream and work with clients across the Okanagan, including West Kelowna.

ABC Appliance and Cool Runnings show how I handle local service businesses. Okanagan Treehouse shows the care I put into presenting accommodation. Where the brief calls for it, branding, video and AI implementation can sit alongside the website work.

For a first conversation, bring: the services you want to promote, who you serve, the area you cover and what you want a visitor to do next. From there I can help shape a page plan, visual direction and a custom quote. See my website design work.

Twin Creek Media is worth a look when a West Kelowna business wants ongoing strategy, creative and advertising wrapped around the website. Its public offer reads as a marketing-department partnership, which is a different decision than a one-off build.

Ask about: how the website fits the wider programme, how campaigns are planned and how enquiries tie back into reporting. An established business with steady marketing needs should weigh the team model and level of commitment against the website work itself. See Twin Creek Media’s approach.

TheBomb is a reasonable option to review for a West Kelowna custom website that needs hosting and support. Its Okanagan offer brings together design, SEO and managed website services.

Ask about: the booking or enquiry system you already use, what content has to be migrated and the changes you expect after launch. A hospitality or seasonal business should be clear about who will update hours, offers and practical visitor information. Make sure those tasks are covered in the proposed support arrangement. Review TheBomb’s service scope.

Twirling Umbrellas is a useful comparison for organisations weighing a more involved WordPress project. Its published focus includes non-profits, associations and regulators, with resource libraries, integrations and content management among the capabilities it describes.

Ask about: how many people will edit the site, approval processes, member or resource information, accessibility and migration. An organisation with complex content needs should look at that experience directly. Explore Twirling Umbrellas’ work.

A West Kelowna website brief should say whether customers are arranging local work, planning a visit or using an organisation’s services. Those journeys need different content and different proof from a designer.

What to request in the proposal
ProjectAsk the provider to explain
Trade or home serviceCoverage, service pages, local proof and quote handling
Winery or accommodationVisitor information, imagery, dates and booking handoff
Community organisationContent ownership, resources, accessibility and updates

For visitor businesses, the official West Kelowna tourism information gives useful context about the area’s wine and outdoor experiences. Your own site still needs to answer the practical questions about your particular offer.

Ask for a relevant example, then follow its customer journey on your phone. Visual quality matters, and so does being able to find the details and finish the task.

A West Kelowna website quote should make clear who creates the content, which integrations are included and who maintains the finished site. Where the provider is based is only one part of the working relationship.

Give each shortlisted firm the same brief: the customer action you want, essential pages, available images, budget range, booking tools and update needs. Then ask how the provider will test the mobile experience and hand over account access.

My West Kelowna website guide goes deeper into the local content decisions. The website cost checklist helps compare proposals before you commit.

faqs: Does the designer need a West Kelowna office?

No. This shortlist includes Okanagan providers for West Kelowna businesses; it is not a claim that every firm has a West Kelowna office. Confirm availability, communication and meeting arrangements alongside portfolio relevance.
What should I ask a designer about a winery or accommodation site?
Ask how imagery, practical visitor information, availability and booking conditions will work together. Review the complete mobile route into the booking platform, not just the homepage design.
Can one provider handle the website and ongoing marketing?

Yes, when those services are included in the agreed scope. Michael McKerracher offers website, marketing and branding work. Compare the build fee, ongoing work, reporting and ownership terms separately so the arrangement is clear.
